sla.title: Remediation deadlines
sla.dialog_help: Days to fix a finding, counted from first detection, for every repository. Leave a field empty so that severity never comes due. Defaults: 7, 30, 90 and 180 days.
sla.invalid: Each due date is a whole number of days from 1 to 3650, or empty to leave it unset.

cra.title: We sell products with software in the EU (CRA)
cra.on: On · CRA reporting kit in Compliance
cra.help_on: Compliance shows the CRA kit: mark your products, assess each KEV match and track the 24 h, 72 h and 14-day deadlines.
cra.help_off: The CRA kit is hidden and no events open. Products and decisions are kept for when you turn it back on.
cra.reason_placeholder: e.g. we sell the mobile app in the EU
cra.reason_short: Give a reason of at least {{min}} characters.
cra.saved_off: Saved. CRA reporting is off; its data is kept.

help.title: How policies apply
help.sla: Deadlines apply to every repository, the Overview and reports. The clock runs on open findings; fixed ones and approved exceptions never come due.
help.secrets: Secret detection defaults apply to every repository scan and PR review. A repository's own .gitleaks.toml is ignored, so a PR can't weaken detection.
help.repository: A repository can add its own entries from Findings, never remove a default.
help.critical: An exposed secret is always critical.
help.admin_only: Only an admin can change them.
help.cra: Turn on CRA reporting only if you sell products with software in the EU; it's off by default.
